newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight closes off high in tight, thin market.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight closes off high in tight, thin market.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate ended at 7.80/8.00 percent after trading at 8.50/70 percent for most of the afternoon as the market tightened after payment for a 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue, dealers said.
They said the 30-day Bank Negara bill issue had created a temporary funds flow mismatch. A 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue is maturing on Friday.
In addition, the market was thin in the first post-festival holiday session with many dealers still away. Many large banks were short of funds, the dealers said.
Malaysian banks were closed from February 7 to 11 for the Chinese Lunar New Year and the Moslem Eid al-Fitr.
An estimated three billion ringgit has temporarily left the banking system, mostly in cash, for the festivals.
"Even after the festivals, people believe it will take about two weeks for the money to come back into the system," one dealer said.
In the morning, however, short-term interbank rates fell as the pressure eased slightly after the festival holidays.
They said the one-week interbank rate was at 7.45/55 percent against 8.30 last Thursday, two-week was at 7.40/45 percent against 7.80 and one-month was steady at 7.35/40 percent.
Three-month and six-month were unchanged at 7.35/40 percent.
"Banks wanted to be long over the long holiday period and the overnight was very high last week, which is why the one-week rate rose so much last Thursday," a Malaysian bank dealer said.
He said the market was very quiet as many dealers were still away on holiday.
